extra.message: username and password from the login request (LoginServlet, LoginAPI, ApiAuthFilter, CCApplyServlet) are concatenated directly into the SQL query used for authentication. An input like `' OR '1'='1' --` lets an attacker bypass authentication entirely or enumerate credentials. The code comment on this line even acknowledges the lack of sanitization.

A hardcoded backdoor credential (username 'jsmith' / password 'demo1234') always authenticates successfully regardless of the actual stored password, bypassing normal authentication and any password change for that account.

username is concatenated directly into a SQL query. Reachable with fully attacker-controlled input via OperationsUtil.getUser(), which decodes the username straight from the client-supplied Authorization header and passes it here unsanitized.
username is concatenated directly into the SQL query building the accounts list, with no parameterization.
username and acctType (from AdminServlet's addAccount form fields) are concatenated directly into an INSERT statement, allowing SQL injection.

username, password, firstname and lastname are concatenated directly into an INSERT statement. Reachable unauthenticated-role via AdminAPI.addUser (POST /api/admin/addUser), which performs no admin-role check before calling this.

username and password are concatenated directly into an UPDATE statement, allowing SQL injection. Reachable via AdminAPI.changePassword (POST /api/admin/changePassword), which performs no admin-role check.

startDate/endDate, taken verbatim from the JSON body of AccountAPI.getTransactions (POST /api/account/{accountNo}/transactions), are concatenated into the WHERE clause without sanitization, allowing SQL injection (e.g. startDate = "2020-01-01' OR '1'='1").

name is concatenated directly into the INSERT statement. OperationsUtil.sendFeedback (OperationsUtil.java:122-125) SQL-escapes email/subject/comments via StringEscapeUtils.escapeSql but never escapes name, leaving it fully SQL-injectable from the public feedback form/API.

changePassword and addUser (lines 25-26, 56) perform no check that the caller is an administrator — the comment explicitly states 'Don't really care if the user is admin or not'. Any user who can pass ApiAuthFilter (i.e. any valid logged-in user) can change ANY other user's password, including the admin account, or create new accounts via POST /api/admin/changePassword and /api/admin/addUser.

AdminFilter (which enforces Role.Admin, see AdminFilter.java:66) is mapped to the misspelled url-pattern '/adimn/*' instead of '/admin/*'. As a result it never actually applies to the real admin endpoints (/admin/addAccount, /admin/changePassword, /admin/addUser in AdminServlet.java), which are protected only by AuthFilter (mere login check). Any authenticated non-admin user can invoke these admin-only operations.

getAccountBalance fetches the account purely by the path parameter accountNo via Account.getAccount(accountNo), with no check that the account belongs to the authenticated caller. The code's own comment states: 'not checking the account number, side privilege escalation possible'. Any authenticated user can read any other user's balance by iterating account IDs.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: showLastTenTransactions retrieves transactions for any accountNo path parameter via getLastTenTransactions()->DBUtil.getAccount()/getTransactions() with no ownership check against the authenticated user, allowing any logged-in user to view another user's transaction history by guessing/enumerating account numbers.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: fromAccount is read directly from the client-supplied JSON body and passed straight through OperationsUtil.doApiTransfer to DBUtil.transferFunds as the debit account, with no verification that the account belongs to the authenticated user (DBUtil.transferFunds only checks the account exists, see DBUtil.java:303-364). An attacker can transfer funds out of ANY account by supplying its account ID as fromAccount.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: doServletTransfer resolves the debit account from the client-supplied 'AltoroAccounts' cookie (Account.fromBase64List(altoroCookie.getValue())) rather than the server-authoritative user.getAccounts(). Since the cookie is just base64-encoded plaintext (Account.java:76-103) with no integrity protection, an attacker can forge the cookie to include another user's account ID/name and transfer funds out of that account, as DBUtil.transferFunds never re-validates ownership.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: getFeedback builds a JSON response by directly concatenating feedbackDetails.getName()/getEmail()/getSubject()/getMessage() into a string without HTML or JSON-string escaping. These fields are fully attacker-controlled via the public feedback submission endpoint (sendFeedback), and OperationsUtil.sendFeedback only SQL-escapes email/subject/comments (not name, and not for HTML) before storage, so a payload like <script>...</script> submitted as the name is stored and later reflected verbatim.

request.getParameter("txtEmail") is concatenated directly into the HTML content string and written to the response via response.getWriter().write(content) with contentType text/html, with no encoding/escaping. A request to survey_questions.jsp?step=done&txtEmail=<script>alert(1)</script> reflects the payload directly into the page.
The user-supplied cleartext password is written to the application log on every failed login attempt via Log4AltoroJ.getInstance().logError, exposing credentials to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The admin login password 'Altoro1234' is hardcoded in source and compared directly, granting admin-session privileges (SESSION_ATTR_ADMIN_KEY) to anyone who supplies it. It cannot be rotated without a code change and is visible to anyone with source access.

checkLogin unconditionally returns {"loggedin":"true"} without inspecting the session or any credential, regardless of whether the caller is actually authenticated — misrepresenting authentication state to any client relying on this endpoint.

getUser decodes the username/password pair from the Authorization header, which (per LoginAPI.java:73-75 and ApiAuthFilter.java:53-63) is just the username and cleartext password Base64-encoded — not encrypted. Base64 is trivially reversible, so these 'tokens' expose plaintext credentials to anyone who intercepts a request, and the same plaintext password is retransmitted on every API call.
